items.followUp: State two contributions of Carolus Linnaeus to biology.

rubric.why: Linnaeus introduced the two-part system for naming organisms.
rubric.description: Identifies his contribution to scientific naming.
rubric.how: Award for naming binomial nomenclature or describing the two-word scientific naming system.

rubric.why: Linnaeus also contributed to the systematic classification of organisms.
rubric.how: Award for stating that he developed or advanced a system for classifying organisms.

modelAnswer: Carolus Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature, in which each organism is given a two-word scientific name.
He also developed a systematic method for classifying organisms.

items.followUp: Give two differences between the primary and secondary cell walls.

rubric.why: The primary cell wall forms first and is relatively thin and flexible.
rubric.description: States a feature of the primary cell wall.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the primary wall and stating that it forms first, is thin, or is flexible.

rubric.why: The secondary wall is deposited later, is thicker, and may be strengthened with lignin.
rubric.description: States a feature of the secondary cell wall.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the secondary wall and stating that it forms after growth, is thicker, or contains lignin.

modelAnswer: The primary cell wall is formed first while the cell is growing; it is thin and flexible.
The secondary cell wall is deposited inside the primary wall after cell growth; it is thicker and often strengthened with lignin.

items.followUp: What is the difference between disjunction and non-disjunction during cell division?

rubric.why: Disjunction is the normal separation of chromosomes or chromatids during cell division.
rubric.description: Defines disjunction as normal chromosome separation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that chromosomes or chromatids separate normally, typically moving to opposite poles.

rubric.why: Non-disjunction occurs when chromosomes or chromatids fail to separate properly, potentially producing cells with an abnormal chromosome number.
rubric.description: Defines non-disjunction as failed or improper chromosome separation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that separation fails or that the resulting cells can have an abnormal chromosome number.

modelAnswer: Disjunction is the normal separation of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to opposite poles during cell division.
Non-disjunction occurs when homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids fail to separate properly, causing an abnormal chromosome number in the resulting cells.
